title: Grading the Grid: A Diabetic Screening Set

patient.name: Mr Rajendran s/o Kumar
patient.presenting_complaint: Attending diabetic eye screening; no visual complaints
patient.address: Blk 210 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, #05-123, Singapore 560210

history.hpc: Referred from the polyclinic diabetic registry (SiDRP) for annual retinal photography and grading. No blurring, floaters, or distortion. Last screening 14 months ago was graded R0M0.
history.pmhx: Type 2 diabetes 12 years, last HbA1c 8.1%. Hypertension.
history.social_hx: Lives with wife; independent in daily activities.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Early nuclear sclerosis both eyes; otherwise unremarkable
examination_findings.fundus: Right eye: several dot-and-blot haemorrhages and microaneurysms in more than one quadrant, with a few hard exudates outside the macula. Left eye: occasional microaneurysms only. No new vessels, no venous beading.

investigations.fundus_photography: Two-field digital colour fundus photographs (macula-centred and disc-centred) captured per SiDRP/SORC protocol for both eyes; images slightly hazy from early cataract but gradable.
investigations.grading_notes: Right eye pattern = moderate NPDR; left eye = mild NPDR. No proliferative features. No exudates or thickening within one disc diameter of the fovea in either eye (no referable maculopathy today).

diagnosis: Moderate non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy right eye, mild NPDR left eye on SiDRP/SORC grading, no maculopathy. No sight-threatening features today; route along the SORC referral pathway at the recommended interval.

immediate: Capture gradable two-field fundus photographs (macula- and disc-centred) for both eyes per SiDRP/SORC protocol
Confirm correct patient/eye labelling and image quality before accepting the set
Apply grading systematically: microaneurysms, dot-blot haemorrhages, hard exudates, venous beading, and new vessels, noting the number of quadrants involved
Assess the macula specifically for exudates or thickening within one disc diameter of the fovea (maculopathy)
Grade each eye (right = moderate NPDR, left = mild NPDR; M0 both) and record the SORC-recommended review/referral interval
Document that early cataract limited image clarity
follow_up: Route the graded set to the reviewing ophthalmologist/senior grader per the SORC pathway
Inform the patient of the screening outcome in lay terms and the next screening interval
Recommend optimisation of glycaemic and blood-pressure control via the diabetic team
patient_education: Explain that diabetic retinopathy is common and often symptomless early, so regular screening matters
Reassure that nothing needing urgent treatment was seen today, but changes were noted that need monitoring
Advise to report any sudden blurring, floaters, or distortion before the next appointment

key_points: Confirms diabetic history, duration, and control (HbA1c)
Confirms referral source (SiDRP diabetic registry) and last grade/interval
Screens for symptoms of sight-threatening disease (distortion, floaters, sudden blurring)
Notes systemic risk factors (hypertension) relevant to retinopathy
Captures gradable two-field fundus photographs per SiDRP/SORC protocol
Verifies correct patient/eye labelling and adequate image quality
Recognises and documents media opacity limiting image clarity
Ensures both eyes are imaged with correct technique/settings for diabetic screening
Applies grading criteria per eye correctly (moderate vs mild NPDR)
Assesses the macula for referable maculopathy (within one disc diameter of fovea)
Distinguishes non-proliferative from proliferative features (no new vessels/venous beading here)
Documents the grade per eye clearly for the reviewing ophthalmologist/senior grader
Routes the set correctly along the SORC referral pathway
Gives appropriate patient education and safety-netting
Reinforces systemic (glycaemic/BP) optimisation via the diabetic team
